newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Private Kazakh bank pioneers ADR/GDR market.
newsitem.headline: Private Kazakh bank pioneers ADR/GDR market.

text.p: Kazakhstan's largest private bank, AB Kazkommertsbank, has become the country's first financial institution to place American and global depository receipts (ADR/GDR) on foreign markets, raising $50.1 million.
"We are pleased to announce the successful closing of the international equity offering of Kazakommertsbank," the bank said in a statement on Thursday.
"The offering...is the first international equity issue by a Kazakh issuer and the first depository receipt programme in the Central Asian republics of the former Soviet Union," it said.

The issue of 2,666,666 ADRs/GDRs, each representing 30 ordinary shares of the bank with a nominal value of 10 tenge, was lead-managed by Global Securities, a regional investment bank based in Istanbul, Turkey.

"The offering was priced at $18.80 per ADR and GDR, the proceeds of the bank being $50.1 million," said Aidan Karibzhanov, deputy head of Global Kazkommerts Securities, the bank's investment branch and a joint venture with Global Securities.
Global Kazkommerts Securities and Dutch bank ING Barings were co-lead managers of the issue.

Karibzhanov said that through the issuance of 80 million new ordinary shares of 10 tenge each Kazkommertsbank had boosted its charter capital by 28 percent. The statement said the capital was now worth 2.83 billion tenge.

After roadshows in June and July in the United States, Asia and Europe, the issue was heavily oversubscribed, with bids from 101 investors totalling around $370 million against the initial offer worth $30 million, Karibzhanov said.
"This is why we had to increase the offer to $50 million," he said.
"The proceeds...will be used to expand the bank's corporate banking operations, as well as to expand its products and services in consumer banking," the statement said.

The receipts, around 50 percent of which were placed in Europe, 30 percent in the United States and 20 percent in Asia among around 60 companies, have been bought by "real 'blue chip' investors", Karibzhanov said. He declined to give company names.
"I can only tell you those are mostly well-known investment funds, asset management companies and investment branches of large industrial companies," he said.
Kazkommertsbank shares are not yet traded in Kazakhstan, which only plans to launch a stock market in autumn.
But the bank said it "intends to list common shares on the Kazakh Stock Exchange and to obtain London Stock Exchange listing for ADRs and GDRs later this year".

Kazkommertsbank, which says it is one of the Central Asian state's best-capitalised banks with total capitalisation of $100 million, was the first Kazakh bank to obtain a credit rating in January, when the U.S. rating agency Thomson BankWatch granted it a rating of B-.

The bank, whose net profit grew last year to 790.1 million tenge from 654.3 million tenge in 1995, said last month its would issue by the end of 1997 three-year Eurobonds worth $100 million. ING Barings has been mandated to lead-manage the issue.
